messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: multiple GPUs reporting CUDA_OOM in eu-west cluster (nodes: gpu-eu-1*, gpu-eu-3*). Headroom metric still >10% across affected nodes. Auto-escalation to on-call
emily-oncall: Acknowledged. Paging on-call now. I’m looking at the recent deploys. Any customers flagged?
emily-oncall: Quick snapshot: 6 nodes showing repeated allocator failures, containers restarting ~1-2x/min. Headroom gauge shows 12-18% free memory reported by runtime. Errors are: `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` in model-server containers.
raj-eng-runtime: Noted. We rolled runtime 1.14.3 -> 1.14.4 last night in eu-west. There was an allocator tweak to reserved-block rounding. Could be related.
ben-sre: grabbing logs. Running `kubectl -n inference logs -l app=model-server -c runtime --since=30m` now. Also pulling dmesg from node gpu-eu-3-2.
ben-sre: log tail: 
```
E 03:12:14 model_runtime.cpp:452 allocation failed: requested 2147483648 bytes
CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY (cuMemAlloc)
Allocator: reserved_pool_total=36GB reserved_pool_free=8GB headroom=12%
```
emily-oncall: Interesting that reserved_pool_free is nonzero. That suggests fragmentation / allocation path mismatch. Any nvml traces?
raj-eng-runtime: Running nvprof/driver introspection. Also check our allocator slab list. Use this script: 
```
# query per-process memory via nvml
python tools/nvml_query.py --pid <pid> --dump-slabs > /tmp/slabs.txt
```
mark-eng: I see frequent small allocations from KV cache on same pids. Could be that KV cache rotated causing many small free blocks and fragmented large contiguous regions.
lisa-ml: We pushed a KV cache change this morning that increased prefix caching to 1.5x. Could that blow up fragmentation? We also increased max_seq to 4096 for a subset of customers.
emily-oncall: For immediate mitigation: proposal:
- Disable KV prefix caching on eu-west runtime via env override (KV_CACHE_ENABLED=false)
- Reduce model max_seq for hosting tier to 2048 temporarily
- Drain and restart the two most noisy nodes (gpu-eu-3-2, gpu-eu-1-4)
- Route traffic away from eu-west to us-east fallback for affected customers
Thoughts?
raj-eng-runtime: +1. Also temporarily increase spare_headroom_percent from 12 -> 25 to avoid future alloc races. That parameter is runtime-config only; can hotpatchs.
ben-sre: Executing drain on gpu-eu-3-2 now: 
```
kubectl drain gpu-eu-3-2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
```
deploy-bot: Routing rule applied: 15% of eu-west load -> us-east fallback models. (route-id: r-9043)
emily-oncall: I applied KV_CACHE_ENABLED=false to the eu-west daemonset (hotpatch). Applied spare_headroom_percent=25 on configmap. Patching rolling restart for runtime pods.
ben-sre: After restart, initial observations: container restarts dropped from ~1-2/min to 0.03/min. Headroom metric still shows ~14% but CUDA_OOM events decreased significantly.
raj-eng-runtime: Good sign. We should still pursue root cause — likely allocator fragmentation + reserved-block allocation strategy changed in 1.14.4 where we prefer exact-fit reserve which fails for large contiguous allocations. Patch idea: change allocator to allow coalescing of adjacent free blocks on free path and fall back to small-block packing.
emily-oncall: Customer impact check: Carlos, can you summarize which customers hit errors?
carlos-support: I have 8 customers alerted: 2 had 502s on inference calls (elevated error rate 4-6%), others saw latency spikes and occasional partial responses. No SLO breaches yet, CS ops emailed affected customers and enabled fallback.
lisa-ml: Confirming we reverted the aggressive KV cache change for eu-west. We'll run a canary with a smaller prefix cache (1.1x) once allocator fix is deployed.
mark-eng: Collected allocator slab dumps from restarted nodes for postmortem. Uploading to internal bucket: https://storage.internal/reports/alloc_slabs/2034567890-slabs.tar.gz
emily-oncall: Next steps agreed:
- raj to prepare a runtime patch (allocator coalesce + configurable reserved-block granularity) and test in canary for 2 days
- SRE to schedule rolling patch and nodes compaction job that triggers free/coalesce on low-traffic windows
- Product to notify customers and update incident page
- Follow-up postmortem scheduled tomorrow 0900 UTC
raj-eng-runtime: Will open a PR referencing this thread and target 1.14.5 with the allocator fix. PR: internal-git/reports/runtime#4521
ben-sre: Creating node drain/rescue playbook entry so oncall can run faster next time.
carlos-support: Posting to status page now: https://status.redwood.company/incidents/2034567890 - mentioned temporary routing & mitigations.
emily-oncall: Handoff: I need to go offline in 30m. Ben will take primary oncall until morning; Raj owns runtime patch. If anything regresses tag me @emily-oncall.
ben-sre: Taking over. I'm monitoring error rates and OOM counts. Current stats: OOMs/hour ~2 (was ~120 before mitigation). Reqs routed to us-east ~12% of traffic.
emily-oncall: Thanks team. We’ll run the postmortem and include clear remediation: runtime patch, KV cache config defaults, and a dashboard for reserved-block fragmentation.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated - reduced OOM events after hotpatch; customer impact limited to 8 customers, two 502 spikes. Follow-up: postmortem scheduled.
raj-eng-runtime: Quick note: root cause hypothesis for postmortem: combination of allocator rounding change + increase in KV prefix cache + higher tail sequence lengths created a workload with many mid-size frees leading to large-fragmentation holes. The runtime thought there was headroom (sum free != largest contiguous), so cuMemAlloc failed. We need a largest-free-extent metric in telemetry.
emily-oncall: logging handoff summary to ops doc and closing this thread after the postmortem. Good job everyone :thumbsup:
